paragraphs.title: The Accusation against Joshua and His Rescue

answers: Before the angel of the LORD
Before the people of the city
easy.explanation: Joshua was standing before the angel of the LORD.
easy.q: Before whom was Joshua the high priest standing?

easy.explanation: Satan stood at Joshua’s right hand to resist him.
easy.q: Who stood at Joshua’s right hand to resist him?

answers: The angel of the LORD only
easy.explanation: The LORD rebuked Satan and defended Joshua and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whom did the LORD defend when He rebuked Satan?

answers: He allowed Satan to judge Joshua
medium.explanation: The LORD rebuked Satan rather than accepting his accusation.
medium.q: What did the LORD do in response to Satan?

answers: He was a piece of wood being burned
He was a remnant rescued from danger and destruction
He was a tool used in the Temple
medium.explanation: The image presents Joshua as someone rescued from the fire of destruction.
medium.q: What does the phrase “a brand plucked out of the fire” suggest about Joshua?

answers: Because Satan was standing in the wrong place
Because Satan wanted to build the Temple
Because the LORD had chosen Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The LORD refers to Jerusalem as the city He had chosen.
medium.q: Why did the LORD rebuke Satan according to the verse?

answers: Accusation and danger contrasted with rescue and protection
A king contrasted with his people
challenge.explanation: The vision shows Satan’s resistance opposed by the LORD’s rescue and protection.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the vision?

answers: God’s protection is greater than the accusation against Joshua
Satan becomes the ruler of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s rebuke shows that Satan’s accusation does not prevail.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Satan’s resistance being answered by the LORD’s rebuke?

answers: As a remnant rescued from danger
challenge.explanation: The phrase “a brand plucked out of the fire” portrays Joshua as one rescued from danger.
challenge.q: How is Joshua portrayed in the LORD’s words?

easy.explanation: Joshua was clothed with filthy garments.
easy.q: What was Joshua wearing at the beginning of the passage?

answers: They were to be taken away
easy.explanation: The angel commanded that the filthy garments be taken away.
easy.q: What did the angel command to be done with the filthy garments?

easy.explanation: A fair mitre was set upon Joshua’s head.
easy.q: What was placed upon Joshua’s head?

answers: The passing away of his iniquity and the renewal of his status
medium.explanation: The angel said, “I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee,” and then gave Joshua new garments.
medium.q: What did the removal of Joshua’s filthy garments represent?

answers: A new set of clean garments
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the new garments given to Joshua after his filthy garments were removed.
medium.q: What does “change of raiment” mean in this passage?

answers: To walk in the LORD’s ways and keep His charge
medium.explanation: Joshua was told to walk in the LORD’s ways and keep His charge.
medium.q: What was required of Joshua after his purification?

answers: The purification enables him to resume his service and responsibilities
The purification turns him into Satan
challenge.explanation: After being purified, Joshua receives responsibilities concerning the LORD’s house and courts.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Joshua’s purification and his public role?

answers: Places to walk among those who stood by
challenge.explanation: The LORD promised to give Joshua places to walk among those standing by.
challenge.q: What would Joshua receive if he fulfilled the stated requirements?

answers: Clean garments, removal of garments, then the commands
Removal of the filthy garments, new garments, then the commands
The commands, Satan’s accusation, then removal of the garments
challenge.explanation: The filthy garments are removed, Joshua receives new garments, and then he is given the conditions for his service.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

paragraphs.title: The Men of Wonder, the Branch, and the Stone

easy.explanation: Joshua and his fellows are called “men wondered at.”
easy.q: What are Joshua and his fellows called in the passage?

answers: The coming of His servant the BRANCH
The coming of a foreign king
easy.explanation: The LORD said that He would bring forth His servant the BRANCH.
easy.q: Whose coming did the LORD announce?

easy.explanation: The verse says that upon the stone there would be seven eyes.
easy.q: How many eyes are mentioned upon the stone?

medium.explanation: The BRANCH is identified in the idea as Zerubbabel.
medium.q: What does the BRANCH represent in the interpretation provided for this passage?

answers: People who serve as a sign or symbol
medium.explanation: The phrase presents Joshua and his companions as significant signs within the prophetic vision.
medium.q: What does “men wondered at” mean in this context?

answers: Zerubbabel’s role in establishing the Temple and removing the land’s iniquity
medium.explanation: The stone is connected with Temple building and the removal of the land’s iniquity.
medium.q: What does the stone with seven eyes symbolize according to the passage’s main idea?

answers: Both are connected with hope and the continuation of Temple building
challenge.explanation: The BRANCH is associated with Zerubbabel, while the stone is linked with the Temple’s restoration.
challenge.q: What connection is formed between the BRANCH and the stone?

answers: The guilt of the land will be taken away
The size of the land will be increased
The Temple stones will be replaced
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to remove the land’s iniquity in one day.
challenge.q: What is the meaning of “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”?

answers: They are connected with the BRANCH, the stone, and the removal of iniquity
They are wearing filthy garments only
challenge.explanation: They are presented as part of a vision pointing to renewal and the removal of guilt.
challenge.q: Why can Joshua and his fellows be viewed as “men wondered at”?

paragraphs.title: Peace and Tranquility on That Day

answers: They will call every man his neighbour
easy.explanation: The verse says that people will call every man his neighbour.
easy.q: What will people do in that day?

answers: Under the cedar and the palm tree
Under the vine and the fig tree
Under the olive and the pomegranate tree
easy.explanation: The verse describes people sitting under the vine and under the fig tree.
easy.q: Under which plants will the people sit?

easy.explanation: The scene represents peace, safety, and restful life.
easy.q: What atmosphere is described in that day?

answers: Cooperation connected with Joshua and Zerubbabel and the removal of the land’s iniquity
medium.explanation: Peace follows the removal of iniquity and the renewal associated with Joshua and Zerubbabel.
medium.q: What makes the time of peace possible according to the main idea?

medium.explanation: Sitting under the vine and fig tree represents safety, welcome, and peaceful rest.
medium.q: What does the invitation to sit under the vine and fig tree symbolize?

medium.explanation: Leisure means having time to rest and live in peace.
medium.q: What does leisure mean in this context?

answers: It shows the result of purification, forgiveness, and renewal
It returns Joshua to his filthy garments
It describes the beginning of Satan’s accusation
challenge.explanation: The peaceful scene presents the result of iniquity being removed and restoration taking place.
challenge.q: How does the final verse connect with the earlier ideas in the chapter?

answers: Peace includes good relationships among people
The people are distancing themselves from one another
challenge.explanation: The invitation shows fellowship, hospitality, and peaceful relationships.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the people calling one another to sit under the vine and fig tree?

answers: From accusation and rescue to purification, renewal, and peace
From peace to accusation and then destruction
From war to exile without any change
challenge.explanation: The chapter moves from the LORD’s protection of Joshua through purification and restoration to peace.
challenge.q: What progression of ideas runs from the beginning to the end of the chapter?
